act_on.finding: Removing `--setting-sources user` makes claude use its default sources (user, project, local), so it loads the branch's `.claude/settings.json` (hooks, env, permissions), `.mcp.json`, CLAUDE.md and skills. Those run with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` in the box. The description's premise is wrong: a read-only mount stops writes, not reads, and the clone is the cwd, so the project scope points at branch-controlled files.
act_on.fix: Restore `--setting-sources user` (and its test), so the host's settings come only through `--settings` and the rulebook through `--plugin-dir`.

act_on.finding: AC1 says the change 'breaks nothing else'. It breaks the invariant, set in #110 and stated in ADR-0012 S12, that the writer loads no branch config. The stated reason (empty user home, read-only clone) does not make the flag redundant, because project-scope settings are read from the clone.
act_on.fix: Revert the removal, or load the settings some other enforced way before dropping the flag.

act_on.finding: The existing test 'runs claude with no settings of the branch…' still expects `--setting-sources user` in the argv, and the diff doesn't edit it. It now fails, and the removed guard has no replacement or stated retirement. Stale references remain at run.ts:5, step.ts:112, agent-settings.ts:7 and GUIDE.md:665.
act_on.fix: Keep the flag; if it were really retired, update the test, the comments and GUIDE.md in the same change.

act_on.finding: Dropping `--setting-sources user` makes claude use its default sources (user, project, local), so it loads the branch's `.claude/settings.json` (hooks, env, permissions), `.mcp.json`, CLAUDE.md and skills. The description's premise is wrong: a read-only mount stops writes but not reads, and the empty user home only covers the user scope. The writer runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, so branch-planted hooks or MCP servers run unattended with the model token in the box.
act_on.fix: Restore `--setting-sources user` (the argv entries removed at this line) so the branch's project and local settings stay unloaded.

act_on.finding: Removing `--setting-sources user` makes claude load its default sources (user, project, local). The writer's cwd is the branch clone, so `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, hooks, `env`, permissions, `.mcp.json`, CLAUDE.md and skills from the branch now load, and the run uses `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. The description's reason is wrong: a read-only mount stops writes, not reads, and an empty home does not affect project-scope settings. This breaks ADR-0012 S12 (config never comes from the branch).
act_on.fix: Restore `--setting-sources user` in claudeArgv.

act_on.finding: The change drops noAgentSettings from the push guards. The read-only mount covers only the agent-setting files the branch already has (agent-settings.ts:3-5). A writer that adds a new .claude/settings.json, .claude/hooks/*, .agents/* or CLAUDE.md in the writer's clone now reaches hostPush with no refusal, and the file lands on the remote branch. The description's premise ('mounts the agent settings read-only already') is false for files the branch lacks.
act_on.fix: Restore noAgentSettings(ci.value) in the `always` guards, or share the one tree walk between both guards without dropping the check.

act_on.finding: AC1 says the change breaks nothing else. Removing the settings guard stops enforcing ADR-0012 S12's rule that agent settings are not changed by a push. The stated perf goal (one tree compare) is not met by deleting a safety check.
act_on.fix: Keep both guards, and get the perf gain by computing the tree walk once and passing it to both.

act_on.finding: The change removes `noAgentSettings` from the push guards, so nothing at the host push now refuses a commit that adds or changes `.claude`, `.agents`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`. The read-only clone mount covers only files the branch already has (agent-settings.ts:3-5). A writer can therefore add a new `.claude/settings.json` or hook and push it, which breaks ADR-0012 S12 (config never comes from the branch).
act_on.fix: Restore `noAgentSettings(ci.value)` in `always`. If the aim is one tree walk, merge the two guards into a single compare instead of dropping one.

act_on.finding: The change drops `noAgentSettings` from the push guards. The description says the clone's read-only mounts make it redundant. But `readOnlyPaths` mounts only the settings paths the checkout already has (clone.ts:153-156). A writer can still add a new `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` that the branch lacked. The host would now push it, because no guard refuses it. That breaks ADR-0012 S12, and the `agent-settings.ts` header says the push wall exists so a file the branch did not have cannot be planted for the next session.
act_on.fix: Restore `noAgentSettings(ci.value)` in `always`. If the two tree walks are the cost, share one walk between `noCiFiles` and `noAgentSettings` instead of removing a guard.

act_on.finding: The change removes a push guard and does not re-establish it elsewhere. The removed guard refused any commit that adds or changes `.claude`, `.agents`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`. The read-only mount covers only paths that already exist, so it does not carry the same contract. Nothing in the change retires the guard on purpose.
act_on.fix: Put the guard back, or add a replacement that refuses new agent-settings files at the push.

act_on.finding: promptFor no longer emits FOREGROUND, so a writer in any mode is not told to run subagents and commands in the foreground. The description says the completion window (#182) makes this unnecessary, but that window only decides a run that hangs after a valid report. A subagent or command left in the background before the report is written is lost (the comment at line 114 says so, #192), and the window cannot recover work that was never reported.
act_on.fix: Restore ${FOREGROUND} in the returned template, or show that the completion window covers background work lost before the report.

act_on.finding: The change leaves two tests asserting the old behaviour, and neither is updated. The test at line 760 expects the prompt to start with the filled template, then FOREGROUND, then PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS. The test at line 777 expects every mode's prompt to include FOREGROUND. Both now fail, so `make test` goes red. The change also gives no test for the new, shorter behaviour.
act_on.fix: Restore FOREGROUND so the tests pass again. If the removal is kept, change both tests on purpose and say why.

act_on.finding: promptFor no longer emits FOREGROUND, so no writer prompt in any mode tells the model to run subagents and commands in the foreground. The constant's own text says a run ends when the model stops and anything left in the background is lost. The completion window (#182) only decides a run that hangs after a valid report. It does not stop the writer losing background work or ending before a background command finishes, so the removed guard (#192) is not replaced.
act_on.fix: Restore ${FOREGROUND} in the returned template, or show why #192's lost-work failure can no longer happen.

act_on.finding: The change leaves existing tests pinned to the old prompt. The test at writer.test.ts:771 expects the prompt to equal text containing FOREGROUND, and line 783 expects every prompt text to include FOREGROUND. Both fail with the new promptFor, so make test is red. The diff also adds no test for the new behaviour.
act_on.fix: Restore the foreground line in promptFor, or update these assertions to the new prompt in the same change.

act_on.finding: The change removes FOREGROUND from every writer prompt, but that line carried a different contract than the completion window. It told the model not to leave subagents or commands in the background, because anything left there is lost when the run ends (#192). The completion window (#182, ADR-0012 S13) only decides a run that hangs after a valid report. It does not recover work a backgrounded subagent had not yet returned when the model stopped. The description's premise therefore covers only part of what the removed text did.
act_on.fix: Restore FOREGROUND in promptFor, or show where the lost-background-work case is handled another way before retiring it.

act_on.finding: The tests still assert the old behaviour and now fail. The prompt-shape test expects `${FOREGROUND}\n\n${PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS}` right after the filled template, and the 'every mode' test at line 783 expects each prompt to include FOREGROUND. promptFor no longer emits it, so both assertions fail for all four modes (fix, test-first, rework, ci). The diff does not touch the tests.
act_on.fix: Restore FOREGROUND in the prompt, or, if the removal is intended, update both tests to assert the new prompt and keep a test that fails if the intended text is dropped.

act_on.finding: AC1 requires that the change 'breaks nothing else'. It breaks the writer tests (F2) and the GUIDE.md contract (F3). It also drops the #192 instruction for all four modes, although the intent says only that the prompt no longer needs to say how to run commands. Removal of the 'lost background work' instruction is not covered by the intent.
act_on.fix: Keep the foreground instruction, or get the spec amended to retire #192 explicitly with its tests and docs.

act_on.finding: The change drops the `readsSystem` guard, so `trustedList(git, "--system", env)` now always runs. An explicit `git config --system` reads the system file even when GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1. With a system file that sets credential.helper and NOSYSTEM=1, hostGit adds that helper back into `trusted`, although the operator turned the system config off. This is the #167 regression.
act_on.fix: Restore the `readsSystem(env)` check (or an equivalent) so the system scope is skipped when GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM is a true value.

act_on.finding: The change removes the readsSystem guard, so readConfig always runs `git config --system --list`. With GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, git skips the system config but an explicit --system still reads it. A system credential.helper therefore lands in `trusted` and hostGit adds back a value the operator turned off (#167).
act_on.fix: Restore the GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM check and skip the system trustedList call when NOSYSTEM is a true value.

act_on.finding: The AGENTS.md MUST says hostGit and hgit must be kept in step. scripts/lib/git.sh:91-99 (hg_nosystem) still skips --system under GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, but hostGit no longer does, so the two now read different trusted config. This also breaks ADR-0012 S12 (no system config in host-side git calls).
act_on.fix: Restore the NOSYSTEM guard in hostGit so it matches hgit.

act_on.finding: readConfig now always reads the system config. With GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and a GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM file that sets credential.helper, `git config --system --list` still returns that file, because explicit --system ignores NOSYSTEM. The helper is added back into `trusted`, so hostGit uses a value the operator turned off (#167).
act_on.fix: Restore the readsSystem(env) guard, so the system list is read only when GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM is not a true value.

act_on.finding: The only criterion is that the change does what the description says and breaks nothing else. The description calls it a refactor, but it removes the NOSYSTEM behavior added for #167. That breaks existing behavior and its test.
act_on.fix: Keep the NOSYSTEM check, or put the behavior change in its own ticket with a spec and updated tests.

act_on.finding: A dead run's worktree that holds uncommitted files or commits no remote branch has is now deleted by remove_worktree (`worktree remove --force`, else `rm -rf`) before the new writer starts, so that work is lost. Input: a claimed MR whose writer died with a local commit or half-done files. Result: start-writer wipes them. The #189 guard that refused this is gone, and reconcile's handoff never gets to see the work.
act_on.fix: Keep the `unlanded_in` check and refuse the start when it reports something, or push or land the work before removing the worktree.

act_on.finding: The tests still assert the old behaviour. The three `expect_fail` cases (lines 76, 84, 90) expect the start to refuse, and the checks that the files stay (lines 78, 86) expect them to survive. With the guard removed, start-writer now starts, so these tests fail. The change updates no test and adds none for the new behaviour, so `make test` goes red.
act_on.fix: Update or remove these cases in the same change, and add a test that pins whatever the new behaviour is meant to be.

act_on.finding: A dead run's worktree that holds uncommitted files or commits no remote branch has (or a folder git cannot check) is now deleted by `remove_worktree` (`worktree remove --force`, else `rm -rf`) with no check. The writer's work is lost. The #189 guard `unlanded_in` is no longer called here.
act_on.fix: Keep the `unlanded_in` check before `remove_worktree`, or push or hand off the dead run's work before removing it.

act_on.finding: The tests at lines 76-91 still assert the old behaviour: a dead run's worktree that git cannot check, with uncommitted files, or with an unpushed commit stops the start and its files stay. This change makes all three start anyway, so `make test` fails. The diff does not update or remove these tests.
act_on.fix: Update or remove the stale assertions in the same change, and add a test for the new behaviour. If the guard stays (F1), these tests are the ones that should pass.

act_on.finding: Input: a dead run's worktree `writer-<iid>` holds uncommitted files or commits no remote branch has. State: the path exists. Result: `remove_worktree` runs `worktree remove --force` or `rm -rf` on it with no check, so the work is destroyed. Before this change `unlanded_in` stopped the start and left it for `reconcile` to land (#189).
act_on.fix: Restore the `unlanded_in` guard so a worktree with unlanded work is kept and the start refuses, or land the work before removing it.

act_on.finding: The change leaves three tests asserting the old behaviour (lines 76-78, 84-86, 90-91). They expect start-writer to fail with 'is not a worktree git can check', 'holds uncommitted files' and 'no remote branch has', and expect the files to stay. After this change the script removes the worktree and starts, so `make test` fails. The diff adds no test for the new behaviour. VB2 and the AGENTS.md rule to write the script and its test together are also unmet.
act_on.fix: Update or remove those assertions to match the intended behaviour, and add a test that fails if the change is reverted.

act_on.finding: The unlanded-commit check `rev-list HEAD --not --remotes` relies on remote-tracking refs, and the added `--prune` at line 314 deletes the ref of any branch the forge has deleted. A writer's branch that was pushed, merged and then deleted by the forge now has its pushed commits listed as unlanded. The ref that used to prove they had landed is gone.
act_on.fix: Drop `--prune` from this fetch, or prune only after the unlanded check, or check landing against the default branch instead of `--remotes`; do the pruning in a separate step that cannot affect the check.

act_on.finding: `fetch --prune` deletes the remote-tracking ref of a branch the forge has deleted, yet `leftIn` (line 326) decides what has landed with `rev-list HEAD --not --remotes`. A writer branch that was pushed, then squash- or rebase-merged and deleted, keeps its commits reachable only through that ref. Once the ref is pruned, those commits count as unlanded.
act_on.fix: Fetch without `--prune`, or prune after the `leftIn` check, or check landing another way, such as against origin's default branch or the change's merge sha. Prune the stale refs in a separate step.

act_on.finding: `fetch --prune` deletes the remote-tracking ref of a branch the forge has deleted, but `leftIn` (line 326) decides what is landed with `rev-list HEAD --not --remotes`. A writer's commits that were landed only by a squash/rebase merge, or whose branch was deleted after merge, were counted as landed through the stale ref. After the prune no ref holds them, so they count as unlanded.
act_on.fix: Do not prune in the fetch that feeds the unlanded-work check. Prune in a separate step after `leftIn` has decided, or test landed commits against the default branch's tip as well as `--remotes`.

act_on.finding: Dropping `--disable` makes curl read the user's ~/.curlrc (and CURL_HOME/XDG config) before the plugin's own `--config`. A ~/.curlrc with `trace`, `trace-ascii`, `verbose`, `dump-header`, `output` or an untrusted `proxy` therefore writes or sends the webhook URL, which the plugin hands curl via a 0600 config file and which the ADR T3 and the file header (lines 3-6) say must never be exposed. `scrubbed()` only cleans curl's stderr, not a trace file or proxy.
act_on.fix: Restore `--disable` as the first curl argument, and if proxy support is needed, read an explicit factory-owned proxy setting (for example pass `--proxy` from a named config) instead of the whole ~/.curlrc.

act_on.finding: The test still asserts `call?.argv[0]` is `--disable`. The change removes that argument, so argv[0] is now `--silent` and the test fails. The stale test pins the old behaviour.
act_on.fix: Replace the assertion with one for the new behaviour, for example that argv has no `--disable`, and update the test name and comment to match.

act_on.finding: AC1 says the change "breaks nothing else". It breaks the existing notify test (F1), and it drops the protection against ~/.curlrc exposing the webhook (F2). The plugin's own docs state that guarantee at lines 2-6 and ADR-0013 T3 supports it. The comment at plugin:2-6 now describes behaviour the code no longer has.
act_on.fix: Fix the test, and either keep the webhook isolation while letting the proxy through or record the accepted trade-off.

act_on.finding: Dropping `--disable` makes curl read the user's ~/.curlrc (and CURL_HOME/XDG config) on every ping. A curlrc with `trace`, `trace-ascii`, `verbose` or `proxy` options can write or route the webhook URL, which is the secret the plugin keeps out of env and argv. Today's flags `--silent --show-error --fail` do not override those options.
act_on.fix: Restore `--disable` as the first curl argument, and add only an explicit proxy option, such as one taken from the request or the factory's own config, if proxy support is needed.

act_on.finding: The guard now matches only `call.plugin === "discord"`. A local plugin added by absolute path under the name `discord`, from any file, passes it and is handed the Discord webhook. The old `sameFile(call.source, bundled)` check was what stopped that, and `plugin-cli.ts:51-64` shows a plugin can come from an absolute path.
act_on.fix: Keep the source check, and make it survive symlinked prefixes by comparing `realpath(call.source)` with `realpath(bundled)`. Today only `bundled` is resolved, so a registered source that is itself a symlink never matches.

act_on.finding: The guard now trusts `call.plugin === "discord"`, which is only a name the registry or project file assigns. Any plugin added from another file under the name `discord` is handed the stored Discord webhook on a notify call, and that is the exact case the old `sameFile` check, which compared the plugin's file with the bundled one, existed to block.
act_on.fix: Keep verifying the plugin's source against the bundled file, comparing real paths on both sides, e.g. `realpath(call.source)` against `realpath(bundled)`, so symlinked prefixes still match without trusting the name.

act_on.finding: The test "a plugin of any name added from another file is never handed it" still expects `{}` for a discord-named plugin whose source is a different file. The change breaks it and the diff does not update it. The criterion says the change breaks nothing else, and this does.
act_on.fix: Restore the source check so the test passes. Do not delete or weaken the test.

act_on.finding: The guard now trusts `call.plugin`, which is the name a plugin gives itself. A plugin added from any other file that calls itself `discord` (input: `{plugin:"discord", capability:"notify", source:"/home/x/discord/plugin"}`) now gets the Discord webhook, where before it got `{}`. That is the case the removed `sameFile` check and the comment on lines 114-116 exist to stop.
act_on.fix: Keep a source check, but compare the real paths of both sides (`realpath(source)` and `realpath(bundled)`), so a symlinked prefix still matches. Or compare against the pinned sha256.

act_on.finding: The test "a plugin of any name added from another file is never handed it, though it calls itself discord" still asserts the old behaviour. With the change, `secrets({plugin:"discord", capability:"notify", source:"/home/x/discord/plugin"})` returns the webhook, not `{}`, so the test fails. No test covers the symlinked-prefix case the change is for.
act_on.fix: Keep this assertion and fix the code (F1). Add a test where `source` is the realpath of a symlinked bundled path and the secret is handed over.

act_on.finding: AC1 says the change "breaks nothing else". It drops the guarantee that only the bundled discord plugin receives the webhook, which nothing in the description or spec asks for. The description only asks that a symlinked prefix match.
act_on.fix: Fix the path comparison (F1) and leave the source restriction in place.

act_on.finding: killGroup now sends SIGKILL to the leader pid only. A plugin that starts a helper (for example `sh -c 'sleep 1000 & wait'`) and runs past the timeout or cap has its leader killed, but the helper survives. The helper keeps the stdout and stderr pipes open, so 'close' never fires and the promise never resolves. The helper also keeps running and writing after the call, which the 'never outlives its call' contract forbids.
act_on.fix: Keep the plugin in its own process group and kill `-pid`. To survive Ctrl-C, handle SIGINT in the parent and forward it. Otherwise resolve on 'exit' and destroy the pipes.

act_on.finding: The criterion says the change 'breaks nothing else'. The change drops the guarantee that a timeout or cap kills the whole plugin tree. That breaks callers of runPlugin, which assume that no plugin write goes on after a timeout or cap. It also leaves the call hanging when a grandchild holds the pipes.
act_on.fix: Meet the Ctrl-C goal without giving up the tree kill. For example, keep the group and forward the terminal signals.

act_on.finding: killGroup now signals only the plugin's own pid, not its process group. A plugin that is a shell script or wrapper and starts a child (e.g. `sleep`, a CLI, a background writer) is killed on timeout or cap, but the grandchild keeps running and can keep writing. The function's comment says it kills 'the plugin and every process it started', and the head comment says a plugin never outlives its call. Neither holds any longer.
act_on.fix: Keep `detached: true` and `process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL")`, and handle Ctrl-C by forwarding SIGINT or SIGTERM to the group. Or another way to kill the whole tree.

act_on.finding: Line 32 now signals only the plugin's own pid, and `detached: true` was dropped, so grandchildren stay alive. For example, a plugin script that runs `sleep 1000 &` or `gh` and then times out or hits the cap is killed on its own while the grandchild keeps running. Before, `process.kill(-pid)` killed the whole group, and the header comment promises that a plugin never outlives its call.
act_on.fix: Keep the plugin in its own process group (`detached: true` and `process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL")`), and handle the Ctrl-C case separately, for example by forwarding SIGINT from the parent.

act_on.finding: Input: a ping for a GitLab project, a ping on a host with no `gh` login, or a `gh` run in the wrong cwd. `gh` fails and `.catch` returns undefined, so the title is "" and the ping still goes out with an empty `title:` field. A repo other than the one the ping is about is also possible, because the call sets no cwd or `--repo` and the PR number is looked up in whatever repository the process runs in. That can put a different PR's title in the ping.
act_on.fix: Resolve the title through the project's forge seam, which knows the repo, and leave the field out when no title is read.

act_on.finding: AC1 says the change breaks nothing else. pluginNotify previously ran offline and was pure up to the plugin call. It now awaits a subprocess with no timeout on every ping, so a hung `gh` stalls the dispatcher tick that awaits the notify. It also calls a forge that is not the project's forge.
act_on.fix: Read the title through the forge seam with the usual timeout and error handling, and never block the ping on it.

act_on.finding: The `gh` call has no `cwd`, no repo flag and no timeout. With a change number such as 12 and a process cwd outside the project's clone, or in another repo, it reads the wrong PR's title or fails. A slow or hung `gh` blocks the ping, so a needs-you ping can go out late or never.
act_on.fix: Read the title through the project-aware Forge seam, which knows the repo, and give the call a timeout.

act_on.finding: The `gh` call has no repo argument and runs in the process cwd. Input: a ping for a GitLab project, or a project whose clone is not the cwd. Result: gh fails or reads another repo's PR with the same number, and the catch returns "". The ping then goes out with an empty or wrong title field, so "carries the change's title" is not met and no error is reported.
act_on.fix: Read the title through the project's Forge adapter, which knows the repo and forge, and surface a read failure instead of sending an empty field.

act_on.rule: AGENTS.md MUST: call git on a project's clone only through hgit or hostGit
act_on.finding: plainFetch runs plain `git -C <repo> fetch` through execFile on the project's clone. hostGit's config reads were what refused hooks, programs and helpers planted in the repo's own config. A planted `core.fsmonitor`, `credential.helper` or `url.*.insteadOf` in the clone's config now runs or applies on the host, with no trusted PATH check and no GIT_CONFIG_COUNT check. This is the exact case the MUST forbids.
act_on.fix: Revert fetchStart to `git(setup.env, setup.repo, ["fetch", ...])` through hostGit. If the three config reads are too slow, speed up hostGit for every caller instead of bypassing it for one.

act_on.finding: AC1 says the change breaks nothing else. The fetch now ignores setup.env, so a caller-supplied env (such as GIT_CONFIG_COUNT overrides, auth or PATH) no longer reaches it. It also drops the hostGit neutralizers that ADR-0012 S12 requires on every host-side git call. A branch or writer can plant config in the clone that the removed guard used to catch.
act_on.fix: Run the fetch through hostGit with setup.env as before.

act_on.rule: AGENTS.md MUST: call git on a project's clone only through hgit or hostGit
act_on.finding: plainFetch runs plain `git -C <repo> fetch` through execFile on the project's clone (setup.repo). The clone's own config can hold hooks, fsmonitor, a custom ssh/proxy command or drivers. This git call runs them as the operator, outside any box, and it has no hardening, no neutral env and no timeout.
act_on.fix: Call hostGit for the fetch as before. If the three config reads are too slow, speed up hostGit itself, for example by caching the reads, and do it for hgit too so the two stay in step.

act_on.rule: AGENTS.md MUST: git on a project's clone only through hgit or hostGit
act_on.finding: plainFetch runs plain `git -C <repo> fetch` through execFile on the project's clone. A program that a branch or writer planted in the repo's config (core.fsmonitor, core.sshCommand, a gitproxy, a credential helper) runs as the operator outside any box. Only hostGit neutralizes those keys, uses a trusted PATH and sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0.
act_on.fix: Call git(setup.env, setup.repo, ["fetch", ...]) (hostGit) again and delete plainFetch; if the fetch is too slow, speed up hostGit's config read instead of bypassing it.

act_on.finding: AC1 says the change must break nothing else. plainFetch drops the ADR-0012 S12 guarantee that every host-side git call runs with hooks off and neutralized config. It also ignores setup.env, so the caller's env no longer reaches the fetch.
act_on.fix: Keep the fetch on hostGit with setup.env, as the line it replaced did.

act_on.rule: AGENTS.md MUST: Give no LLM seat a forge token
act_on.finding: Adding GH_TOKEN and GITLAB_TOKEN to CLAUDE_ENV makes claudeEnv() pass the host's forge token to the claude CLI. That CLI runs the reviewer finder and the review sessions, so an LLM seat that reads untrusted PR text now holds a forge token. ADR-0012 S2, S6 and S11 forbid this.
act_on.fix: Remove both names from CLAUDE_ENV. If the finder needs old comments, have the host fetch them through the Forge seam into the pack.

act_on.rule: AGENTS.md MUST: Give no LLM seat a forge token or a skip-permissions flag in new code (ADR-0012 S2, S6, S11)
act_on.finding: Adding GH_TOKEN and GITLAB_TOKEN to CLAUDE_ENV makes claudeEnv() copy the host's forge token into the environment of the claude CLI that runs the finder. That gives an LLM seat, which reads untrusted PR text, a live forge credential.
act_on.fix: Remove both names from CLAUDE_ENV and put the older comments into the pack, which the host builds through the Forge seam.

act_on.rule: AGENTS.md MUST: Give no LLM seat a forge token
act_on.finding: Adding GH_TOKEN and GITLAB_TOKEN to CLAUDE_ENV means claudeEnv() passes the host's forge token to the claude CLI. The finder and the other sessions built from claudeEnv are LLM seats that read untrusted PR text, so this breaks the rule that no LLM seat gets a forge token (ADR-0012 S2, S6, S11).
act_on.fix: Remove both names from CLAUDE_ENV. If the finder needs older comments, have the host fetch them through the Forge seam and add them to the pack.

act_on.finding:
The paragraph split `/
[ 	]*
/` eats only two newlines per match, so an odd run of blank lines (3 newlines, two blank lines) before the trailers leaves a leading empty line in the last paragraph. Input `fix: x


Agent: writer` gives last paragraph `
Agent: writer`. The empty line counts as `other=1`, `all` is false, and `gitWritten` is false, so commitKind returns person instead of agent. Git treats several blank lines as one separator and reads this as a trailer block.
act_on.fix: Split on `/\n(?:[ \t]*\n)+/` so any run of blank lines is one separator, or drop empty lines from the last paragraph.

act_on.finding: The change turns `size > maxBytes` into `size >= maxBytes`, so a plugin that prints exactly maxBytes bytes is now killed as overCap. The contract says output "may hold at most maxBytes bytes", so exactly maxBytes must be allowed. Example: maxBytes=100 and the plugin writes 100 bytes. Then size=100, 100>=100 is true, the group is killed, and the result is overCap instead of exited. It also reports `printed more than 100 bytes` (registry.ts:155) when it printed exactly 100.
act_on.fix: Restore `size > input.limits.maxBytes`, so only output past the cap is cut.
